item.title: 22 History of Purāṇa Literature
item.description:
[[P815]]SECTION IV

THE PURĀ[[NAS|ṆAS]] AND DHARMAŚĀSTRA

CHAPTER XXII

Origin and development of Purāṇa literature

The History of Dharmaśāstra (vol[[ |.]][[I| I]] pp. 160-167[[ )|)]] has a [[hrief|brief]] chapter on the [[Puranas|Purāṇas]]. It has been shown [[tharsin|therein]] how the Taittir[[iya|īya]] [[Arapyaka|Āraṇyaka]], the Ch[[a|ā]]ndogya and Bṛ[[ba|ha]]d[[a|ā]]raṇyaka Upani[[s|ṣ]]ads mention Itih[[a|ā]]sa and Pur[[a|ā]]ṇa (sometimes [[callectively|collectively]] as ‘Itih[[a|ā]]sapurā[[da|ṇa]]m’ and sometimes separately as ‘Itih[[i|ā]]saḥ Purā[[pa|ṇa]]m’) and how some of the extant P[[a|u]]rāṇas are [[minch|much]] [[varlier|earlier]] than the 6th century A.D. It is further pointed out there that the number of the principal Pur[[anag|āṇas]] has been traditionally handed down as eighteen,1 that some [[para as much|purāṇas such]] as the Matsya, the Vi[[s|ṣ]][[p|ṇ]]u, the V[[a|ā]]yu and Bhaviṣya contain [[mich|much]] Dharm[[s|a]]-śāstra material, that the Garuḍa-purā[[na|ṇa]] and the Agnipur[[na|āṇa]] contain several [[bundred|hundred]] verses each that are identical with [[verste|verses]] of the Yājñavalkya [[amrti|smṛti]], that there is great divergence as to the extent of almost all Pur[[apa|ṇa]]s, that some of the P[[a|u]]rāṇas [[that selves|themselves]] enumerate minor works called Upapur[[aba|āṇa]]s, that the Purāṇas are divided into three groups, [[vis|viz.]] sātt[[laku|vika]], r[[a|ā]]jasa and tāmasa (as done by Garuḍa [[L|I.]] 223. 17-20, and Padma [[VL.|VI.]] 263. 81-84). Details were also f[[a|u]]rnished as to the chapters of the Pur[[a|ā]]ṇas in which the several topics of Dharmaśāstra ([[ch|such]] as ācāra, āhnika, d[[a|ā]]na, r[[ö|ā]]jadharma, [[f|śr]]āddha, tīrtha) were dealt with.

item.title: 23 Notes on Purāṇas and Upapurāṇas
item.description:
[[P887]]CHAPTER XXIII

Brief Notes on individual Purāṇas and Upapurāṇas

Agnipurāṇa—‘Present Agni’ (by H.) in [[L.|I.]] H. Q. vol. [[Xi|XII]] pp. 683-691; ‘Studies in genuine [[Agneya|Āgneya]] alias Vahnipurāṇa’ by H. in ‘Our Heritage’ vol. I part 2 pp. 209–245 and vol. II part 1 pp. 76-109; ‘Discovery of genuine [[Āgneyapurāṇa ‘|Āgneyapurāṇa’]] by [[E.|H.]] in J. O. [[L|I.]] (Baroda) vol. V (1956) pp. 411-416 (shows that present Agni published by [[Anan.|Ānan.]] Press is not the original [[Purana,|Purāṇa,]] that this was compiled late, while the original [[Agneya|Āgneya]] or Vahni is not yet printed); the Dānasāgara p. 7. verse 63 speaks of an Āgneya which it has discarded apart from one which it has utilized (p. [[% Vorso|2 verse]] 11). As usual with most Purāṇas, the printed [[Agneya|Āgneya]] glorifies itself by saying (in chap. 272. 13 and 17) that in that Mahāpurāṇa Hari resides in the form of [[diffe rent|different]] lores and the Āgneya is a great purāṇa full of Veda and all vidyās.
